entities.title: The same inputs give the same game
entities.summary: The sim is deterministic on every platform.
entities.requirement: Rule code uses f64 with only + − × ÷ and sqrt, plus the functions RULES names, and draws random numbers only from its own seeded generators, so a replay gives the same state everywhere and a later server can run the same sim.
entities.measuredBy: The use case's test that two runs with the same input end in identical states, and the parity replays.

entities.title: Dependencies point inward
entities.summary: Presentation → use cases → features → capabilities; capabilities depend on nothing further out.
entities.requirement: Within lodestar-core no capability uses a feature or use case and no feature uses a use case; the crate graph keeps Godot, infrastructure and the bridge out of lodestar-core.

entities.title: No deferred-work markers
entities.summary: Wanted work is a ⚠️ or ❌ in the owning document, never a comment marker.
entities.requirement: No tracked source file holds a comment that opens with one of knowledge-driven development's four deferred-work words, and there is no deferred-work folder.

origin.description: DESIGN § Testing, the deferred-work gate; AGENTS.md § LodeStar.

entities.title: A stall never runs a burst of ticks
entities.summary: The sim runs at 12 ticks a second whatever the frame rate, and a long frame is cut to a quarter of a second.
entities.requirement: TickClock turns frame time into whole 12 Hz ticks and cuts any frame longer than MAX_FRAME_SECONDS, so a stall runs at most three catch-up ticks.
entities.measuredBy: The use case's tests of the tick clock.

entities.title: 60 fps in the busiest bubble
entities.summary: The worst case, twelve ships fighting near the sun with every effect, holds 60 fps.
entities.requirement: A release build holds 60 fps at 1920×1080 on the High preset on an M1 MacBook Air in the busy-bubble scene.
entities.measuredBy: The busy-bubble benchmark of DESIGN § Testing, a scripted scene not yet built.
